matches.quote: one from resonant tunnelling through the level, one from tip-induced ionisation or charging in a double-barrier geometry.
The abstract and introduction frame the work as revealing "how macroscopic coherence emerges from locally collapsed pairing"... but no data near the excitonic transition are presented.
The bands are not shown to represent Ta2Pd3Te5's quasi-1D, multi-orbital, spin-orbit-coupled band structure, including its proposed Dirac/topological character (refs. 6, 22).
Show the defect-free gap magnitude in type-I versus type-II regions; if the order parameter is locally reduced, the gap should be smaller.
state the setpoint, the number of vacancies per type, the number of tips and cleaves, and whether the histograms are corrected for setpoint.
Vacancies are identified from topography with a cluster-decorated tip (Fig. 2a,b, Fig. S2), and appear as "elongated protrusions", which is unusual for a missing chalcogen atom.
No DFT-simulated STM images, formation-energy considerations or controlled defect creation/annealing are presented.
The "Note added" cites Kwon et al. (ref. 41). A short discussion of agreements and differences, for example in defect types, energies and interpretation, would help readers.
The mean-field model cannot tell an excitonic condensate from an ordinary hybridization (band) insulator, so it cannot support the pair-breaking assignment, and the concluding claim is circular.
The text argues that the vacancy-dependent 2δ (Fig. 2d) "highlights their origin from the e–h pair-breaking states". Bound-state energies of any defect depend on its local configuration.
The regions are defined by a modest shift of a single normal-state feature near +120 to +130 meV (Fig. 4b, black and red arrows).
The bands are not shown to represent Ta2Pd3Te5's quasi-1D, multi-orbital, spin-orbit-coupled band structure, including its proposed Dirac/topological character (refs. 6, 22).
Show whether the gap edges and coherence-like peak of the defect-free region shift by the same amount under the same It sequence
Typos and wording: "formulism" (formalism), "predicated" (predicted), "Yu-Yhiba-Rusinov" (ref. 37), "those … tends", "a specific orbital".
The tip-decoration procedure and its effect on spectra should be described, including whether spectra were taken with a normal or a decorated tip.

notes: P13 and P18 are section header strings ('Suggestions for improvement') rather than distinct technical points. C15 (dynamical Coulomb blockade across tip-impurity-sample junctions) is marked 'partly' under P8, which proposes charging in a double-barrier geometry and looking for charging contrast in dI/dV maps. C10 and C12 are marked 'partly' under P17, which notes that the toy two-band model ignores the Dirac/topological character of Ta2Pd3Te5 but does not specifically discuss massless symmetry protection or Berry phases.
